correctness.rationale: The Kirchhoff path expansion gives K_s(v,v)=(deg(v) sqrt(pi s))^{-1} plus exponentially small walk corrections and off-diagonal exponential decay. Positive-semidefinite Q yields a nonnegative weighted spectral measure whose Laplace transform has coefficient S/sqrt(pi s); Karamata gives N_Q(Λ)~2S sqrt(Λ)/pi. Exact Itô isometry and Abel summation prove the logarithmic S/(2pi), the power coefficient S/[pi(4α-1)], and finite subcritical energy. Gaussian linear-subspace zero-one and Fernique upgrade infinite variance to a.s. non-membership. Integrating F(2s) proves the initial-energy erf law with exponential remainder. The included numerical and exact test checks covariance parity and independent star normalization but is not used as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The motivating primary study proves regularity only below 1/4 and leaves optimality at this natural boundary unresolved in its statement. The new theorem supplies a sharp almost-sure fixed-time threshold for every nonzero correlated vertex covariance on every compact Kirchhoff graph, exact ultraviolet divergence with a universal inverse-degree coefficient, and the complementary short-time energy law. These facts quantify robustness under noisy network branching, not an arbitrary parameter example; no standalone local Weyl theorem or prior subcritical existence is claimed.
